sample_unit: inpatient hospital medicine encounters (discharge summary narratives)

links.outcome: Blinded reviewer quality and preference for LLM versus physician discharge summary narratives
links.effect: Overall quality 3.67 vs 3.77 (p=0.213); preference p=0.270; LLM more concise and coherent but less comprehensive, with more errors (2.91 vs 1.82 per summary).
links.quote: Across 100 encounters, LLM- and physician-generated narratives were comparable in overall quality on a 1-5 Likert scale (average 3.67 [SD 0.49] vs 3.77 [SD 0.57], p=0.213) and reviewer preference (χ2 = 5.2, p=0.270).

links.outcome: Errors (inaccuracies, omissions, hallucinations) and potential harm in LLM-drafted discharge summaries
links.effect: LLM narratives averaged 2.91 errors per summary vs 1.82 for physicians; overall potential harm 0.84 vs 0.36 (p<0.001), though low (<1 on 0-7 scale).
links.quote: LLM-generated narratives contained more unique errors (average 2.91 [SD 2.54] errors per summary) than physician-generated narratives (1.82 [SD 1.94]).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the quality, error types, and safety/potential harm of LLM-generated discharge summary narratives compared to physician-written ones via a blinded reader study, but it does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
